sentences.text: RESPONDENT
(BY SRI RANGASWAMY R, HCGP)

THIS CRL.P FILED U/S.438 CR.P.C PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE  PETITIONERS ON BAIL IN THE EVENT OF THEIR ARREST IN  CR.NO.148/2023 REGISTERED BY KANAKAPURA TOWN POLICE  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:41153  CRL.P No. 11191 of 2023 STATION, RAMANAGARA FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 498A, 304(B) R/W 34 OF IPC AND SECTION 3 AND 4 OF DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT,
PENDING ON THE FILE OF PRINCIPAL CIVIL JUDGE AND J.M.F.C.,
KANAKAPURA, RAMANAGARA.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Accused Nos.2 and 3 in Crime No.148/2023 registered by Kanakapura Town Police Station,
Ramanagara District for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 304(B) R/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 are before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
2.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

3. On the basis of complaint dated 03.09.2023 lodged by Sri Gurumallaiah S/o Late Manchaiah, FIR in Crime No.148/2023 has been registered against Vishal Kumar Sindya and the petitioners herein who are the parents of Vishal Kumar Sindya.
4. In the complaint it is averred that complainant's daughter Smt. Manjula had married accused no.1 about 6 years prior to the date of complaint and the said marriage was a love marriage.
Immediately after the marriage, the couple were living with the petitioners herein.

Subsequently, the NC:
2023:KHC:41153 complainant had arranged a separate residential accommodation for the couple and they were living in the said house along with their son aged about 4 years.
5. It is alleged in the complaint that accused no.1 used to consume liquor and ganja and used to ill-treat his wife Manjula.
On 03.09.2023 at about 3.00 a.m, accused no.1 allegedly informed the complainant that Manjula had committed suicide by hanging.
Immediately, the complainant went to the house of accused no.1 and found the dead body of his daughter.

Thereafter, he had approached Sri Manjunath Rao Sindhya vs State Of Karnataka on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111951168/
2 the police and lodged a complaint which had resulted in registering FIR in Crime NO.148/2023 against Vishal Kumar Sindhya and the petitioners herein.

entities.text: Sri Manjunath Rao Sindhya vs State Of Karnataka on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apprehending arrest in the said case, the petitioners had filed Crl.Misc.No.5297/2023 before the Trial Court which was dismissed on 07.10.2023.
It is under these circumstances, the petitioners are before this Court.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that the complaint lacks necessary ingredients for invoking Section 304B of IPC.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State has opposed the bail application.
8. From a perusal of complaint averments it is seen that the marriage of complainant's daughter with accused no.1 who is the son of petitioners herein was a love marriage.
Though initially the couple were staying with the petitioners herein, subsequently they started staying in residential accommodation which was provided to them by the complainant.

9. In the complaint there is no allegation against the accused persons that there was demand made by them for payment of dowry and in furtherance of such demand they used to ill-treat and harass deceased Manjula.
In the absence of such allegation it becomes doubtful that Section 304(B) of IPC gets attracted against accused persons.
The material on record would go to show that the petitioners are residing separately and they are not residing with accused no.1 and his family.
Under such circumstances, I am of the view that the prayer made by the petitioners for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.
NC: 2023:KHC:41153 Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioners in the event of their arrest in Crime No.148/2023 registered by Kanakapura Town Police Station, Ramanagara District for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 304(B) R/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, subject to the following conditions:
a.

The petitioners shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only)
each with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
b. The petitioners shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
c. The petitioners shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and they shall co-
operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon till filing of charge sheet.
